newsitem.title: NEPAL: Two American climbers killed in Nepal.
newsitem.headline: Two American climbers killed in Nepal.

text.p: Two climbers from the United States died after an avalanche hit them while they were attempting to scale Annapurna IV peak in the Himalayan kingdom of Nepal, a U.S. embassy official said on Sunday.
The official told Reuters that the two climbers were identified as Debbie Marshall, 32, a forester from Glenwood Springs, Colorado, and Richard Davidson, 46, a computer engineer from New Mexico.

An official from Nepal's tourism ministry said the two were among three climbers reported missing on Friday after the avalanche hit them at 4,900 metres (16,072 feet) up the 7,525 metre (24,682 feet) Annapurna IV peak.
A Royal Nepal Army helicopter rescued the third climber, Cleve Armstrong, 52, on Sunday morning from an altitude of 5,200 metres (17,056 feet). He was taken to Nepal's capital Kathmandu.
Armstrong, a doctor from Denver, Colorado, was leading a seven-member expedition.
"As a doctor himself, he (Armstrong) was able to confirm that the other two were dead," the embassy official said. Details about the other group members were not immediately available.
